checks_run: Static review of all 49 submitted files for contract correctness, learner usefulness, progressive disclosure, provenance boundaries, and validation honesty
Filesystem inventory, special-file and symlink inspection, credential-pattern audit replay, and SHA-256 integrity checks
Exact GCC, Binutils, Python, and Make version probes plus the submitted C11 environment probe
Strict warning-as-error builds of the starter, sealed reference, and direct VM safety target in an external scratch copy
Eleven public reference tests, twenty-two sealed black-box tests, twelve direct VM safety tests, and the documented starter baseline
Independent 576-case int64 arithmetic matrix, 160 fixed-seed expression cases, exact resource boundaries, modes, diagnostics, and output-failure checks
Deterministic adversarial-corpus regeneration and execution of all ten generated cases
UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer rebuild and rerun of the sealed, differential, and direct VM checks
Three same-input optimized rebuilds and byte-for-byte binary comparison
Bounded benchmark-harness smoke run without promoting a benchmark label
evidence: GCC 15.2.0 strict builds completed without diagnostics; the reference passed 11/11 public, 22/22 sealed, and 12/12 direct VM tests.
The intentionally incomplete starter reproduced its documented baseline: 3 public tests passed and 8 failed at the compiler stub.
The independent differential harness passed 757 invocations, including 576 arithmetic combinations checked against Python big integers and 160 deterministic generated expressions.
The same independent checks, all 22 sealed tests, and all 12 direct VM cases passed under UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer with no sanitizer diagnostic.
Three optimized reference builds were byte-identical with SHA-256 494ba8d100328e7dc50fe2f17edd8918f96d56186bdbd3355c7a98742f331583.
The regenerated adversarial corpora were identical, and all ten cases produced their specified success or error class.
The learner allowlist contains only guidance, stubs, public tests, and environment helpers; solution implementations, answers, and maintainer tests are segregated under sealed paths.

MANIFEST.yaml honestly limits status to GENERATED and PARTIAL, requires independent validation, and sets productionized=false; the prose consistently disclaims fuzzing, benchmark evidence, transfer, security, production, and acceptance labels.
The reviewed CANDIDATE checksum stream has SHA-256 856fe4df7e21164c32d17b7bae240e7668c3b699f40f5b47a9c5a65135e5e938, and post-test comparison found no submitted-content mutation.
limitations: The immutable catalog baseline and linked upstream repository were unavailable, so source-commit, CC0 catalog evidence, and the claimed absence of copied linked content could only be checked for internal consistency.
Actual student-view projection is orchestrator-controlled; this review verified the declared allowlist and on-disk segregation but could not exercise publication-layer access controls.
The historical no--B linker failure in the candidate validation record did not reproduce because /usr/bin/ld 2.30 was available; the positive, explicitly pinned Binutils 2.43 build did reproduce.
No exhaustive fuzzing, cross-platform transfer, production-readiness, or security certification was performed, and none is claimed.
The benchmark invocation was only a bounded harness smoke check and does not support BENCHMARKED status.
